documents.body: Daughter called early, roads icy and she does not want him on the steps. Cancelled 10:30, rebooked Thu 2/12 at 1:30.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from January. Daughter with him.
Winter has been uneventful. Walking unchanged per daughter, slow but no falls. Bladder unchanged. Memory roughly stable. Knees ache in the cold, acetaminophen helps. Taking everything from the pillbox.

Vitals reviewed, BP at goal. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No swelling of the legs. Short slow steps, rises from chair without using his arms.

Assessment and plan:
1. Hypertension - controlled. Amlodipine 5 mg.
2. Hyperlipidemia, small vessel disease - atorvastatin 20, aspirin 81.
3. NPH - stable per family, neurology following.
4. Knee OA - acetaminophen as needed.
Six months, or sooner with any change in walking or a fall.

documents.title: Dad has fallen
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, Ellen here (Peter's daughter). Over the last couple of months Dad has gone downhill. He has fallen more than once, mostly turning in the kitchen, luckily no injuries. He is misplacing things constantly and asks me the same question several times in an hour. More accidents too, he can't get to the bathroom fast enough. No headaches, no sickness. I called neurology and they have him on June 12. Is there anything we should do before then?

documents.title: RE: Dad has fallen
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Ellen, thank you for letting me know, and I'm glad he wasn't hurt. Please keep the June 12 neurology visit. Until then: someone at his elbow for turns, nightlights on the route to the bathroom, and a urinal by the bed at night may help. If he hits his head, is suddenly much more confused, or can't get up, call 911 or take him to the ED. Let's have him come in to see me after the neurology appointment - the front desk will call with a time.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY GROUP - FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 06/12/2026
Patient: Peter Bowen, 77

Follow-up for normal pressure hydrocephalus; last seen here 12/2024. His daughter accompanies him. Over roughly three months she has seen his memory slip further: he misplaces things and repeats questions. He has fallen several times, and at times he wets himself before he can get to the toilet. He has had no headaches, nausea or intercurrent illness.

Medications: amlodipine 5 mg, atorvastatin 20 mg, aspirin 81 mg, acetaminophen as needed. NKDA.

Exam: Steps are short and hesitant and he needs a hand to stay balanced. Tandem gait is impaired. Mild cognitive impairment on bedside testing. No focal neurologic deficit.

Impression: normal pressure hydrocephalus with progression of gait, cognitive and urinary symptoms.

Plan:
1. Referral to neurosurgery for a high-volume lumbar tap test and evaluation for shunting.
2. Physical therapy for gait and balance; may be arranged locally.
3. Fall precautions discussed with patient and daughter.

cc: primary care

documents.title: Neurology note received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Neurology follow-up note (6/12) received by fax, scanned, routed to PCP. Patient already booked with PCP 6/26.

orders.reason: gait and balance training, fall prevention; normal pressure hydrocephalus

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after neurology 6/12, with daughter.

She counts several falls since spring, all at home, mostly on turns or getting up at night; none with head strike or injury, he has been able to get up with help. Memory worse as she described in May. Bladder accidents more often, before reaching the bathroom. No headache, no fever, no urinary burning. Neurology's plan is neurosurgery for a lumbar tap test and a look at a shunt; their office is making that referral. They suggested PT.
Meds: amlodipine 5, atorvastatin 20, ASA 81, acetaminophen prn. Pillbox by daughter, no missed doses.

Exam: vitals as charted. Comfortable. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. No bruising. Gait: short, hesitant steps, needs my arm for balance on the turn. Strength symmetric. Otherwise nonfocal.

A/P
1. Normal pressure hydrocephalus, progressing - neurosurgery evaluation pending through neurology. Daughter will let us know the date.
2. Recurrent falls - added to problem list. PT referral for gait/balance and home program. Reviewed: clear walkways, nightlights, bedside urinal, shower chair.
3. HTN - controlled; no orthostatic symptoms. Continue amlodipine 5.
4. HLD, small vessel disease hx - continue atorvastatin 20 and aspirin 81.
5. Knee OA - acetaminophen as needed.
Refills sent. Follow-up after the neurosurgery visit, or sooner if another fall.

documents.title: Update on Dad
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick update: PT started last week, twice a week, and he is doing the exercises at home with me. Neurosurgery called and his appointment is in September. No falls since we saw you. Thanks, Ellen

documents.title: RE: Update on Dad
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thanks Ellen, good to hear. Doctor is aware. Send us the exact neurosurgery date once it is confirmed so we can watch for their note.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy asked for refills on aspirin 81 mg and acetaminophen 500 mg (OTC, pharmacy keeps them on profile). Advised OTC, no prescription needed. Amlodipine and atorvastatin have refills on file from 6/26.
